cards.name: Exhaustion
cards.oracle_text: Creatures and lands target opponent controls don't untap during their next untap step.

cards.name: Kefnet's Last Word
cards.oracle_text: Gain control of target artifact, creature, or enchantment. Lands you control don't untap during your next untap step.

cards.name: Mana Vapors
cards.oracle_text: Lands target player controls don't untap during their next untap step.

cards.name: Twincast
cards.oracle_text: Copy target instant or sorcery spell. You may choose new targets for the copy.

cards.name: Unsummon
cards.oracle_text: Return target creature to its owner's hand.

rulings.comment: The creatures and lands are only prevented from untapping during the targeted player’s next untap step. They can still can untap during other player’s untap steps.
No creatures or lands controlled by the player will untap during their next untap step. This includes those which entered the battlefield after Exhaustion resolved.

Gaining control of a creature doesn’t cause you to gain control of any Auras or Equipment attached to it. They’ll remain attached, but an Aura’s effect that affects “you” still affects its controller rather than you, the controller of an Equipment can move it during their next main phase, and so on.

If more than one spell says that lands you control don’t untap during your next untap step, the effects will all wear off during that untap step. You’ll untap lands you control during your untap step after that one.
If the target permanent is an illegal target by the time Kefnet’s Last Word resolves, the entire spell doesn’t resolve. Your lands will untap during your next untap step as normal.
In a multiplayer game, if a player leaves the game, all cards that player owns leave as well, and any effects that give the player control of permanents immediately end.
No lands that you control will untap during your next untap step, even lands that aren’t tapped as this spell resolves. This includes lands that enter the battlefield after this spell resolves.
The control-change effect of Kefnet’s Last Word lasts indefinitely. It doesn’t wear off during the cleanup step.
No land controlled by the player will untap during their next untap step. This includes lands which entered the battlefield after Mana Vapors resolved.
If the spell has damage divided as it was cast, the division can't be changed, although the targets receiving that damage still can. The same is true of spells that distribute counters.
If the spell that's copied has an X whose value was determined as it was cast, the copy will have the same value of X.
If the spell that's copied is modal (that is, it says "Choose one —" or the like), the copy will have the same mode. A different mode can't be chosen.
The copy is created on the stack, so it's not "cast." Abilities that trigger when a player casts a spell won't trigger. The copy will resolve before the original spell does.

The copy will have the same targets as the spell it's copying unless you choose new ones. You may change any number of the targets, including all of them or none of them. If, for one of the targets, you can't choose a new legal target, then it remains unchanged (even if the current target is illegal).
Twincast can copy any instant or sorcery spell, not just one with targets.

You can't choose to pay any alternative or additional costs for the copy. However, effects based on any alternative or additional costs that were paid for the original spell are copied as though those same costs were paid for the copy.

source: Scryfall Oracle/rulings subset for offline tests
